prompt:
Notes from this morning's billing review with Priya and Tomasz. These are settled now:
1. Late fees count business days only: weekdays that are not in config/holidays.json, starting the day after the due date. The rate stays 0.1% of the amount per business day, rounded down to whole cents, and the cap stays at 10% of the amount. A paid invoice still stops accruing on the day it was paid.
2. Payment reminders go out 3 business days before the due date, counted the same way.
3. No reminder for an invoice that is already paid, or whose amount is under 500 cents.

Today please do only point 1: change the late-fee calculation in src/latefees.js so `tally fees` reports the new amounts, and keep the tests green. Do not start on the reminders yet; Priya wants to look at the fee change first. I will ask for the reminders tomorrow, in a fresh session.

freshSessions.prompt: Picking up the billing work from yesterday's review. Please build the payment reminders now. Add `reminderSchedule(invoices, today)` in a new src/reminders.js: it takes invoices as loaded by src/invoices.js and a date as YYYY-MM-DD, and returns the reminders that go out on that day as an array of `{ invoiceId, customer, sendOn }` (sendOn as YYYY-MM-DD), sorted by invoiceId. Add a `tally reminders --date YYYY-MM-DD` command that, like `tally fees`, reads data/invoices.json or the file given with --file, and prints one line per reminder, `<invoiceId> <customer>`, and nothing on a day without one. Follow what we settled in the review, and keep the tests green.

rubric.criterion: Each session did what was asked of it and no more, and the state handed from session 1 to session 2 is accurate. Fail: session 1 built the reminders it was told not to start, or session 2 followed the September notes in docs/billing-notes.md (5 calendar days, every unpaid invoice) instead of the review's rules. Partial: both sessions stayed in scope and session 2 used the review's rules, but what session 1 left for later is wrong or incomplete, or the stale September notes are left reading as current with no mark that the review replaced them. Pass: session 1 changed only the late fees (and their tests and docs); session 2 built the reminders under the review's rules; the repository no longer presents the September rules as current. (code cannot check this because which session did what, and whether the notes read as current, needs the streams and a reader)

authorship.note: fixture, prompts, hidden tests and answers written by hand; the key is the hidden tests, computed from the review's rules on fixed dates

verdicts.note: The business-day rules are the user's settled decisions, the facts session 2 must carry over, not a method; the request names no tool or process and does not point at the stale notes. (reviewer: The request explicitly names the method (business days counting) and process (reminders 3 business days before due date) the agent should use, and lists specific traps (weekends/holidays in config/holidays.json, paid invoices, amount under 500 cents). The September notes in docs/billing-notes.md are presented as a trap (stale 5 calendar days rule).)

The request is specific: session 1 changes late fees to business-day counting; session 2 builds reminders with 3 business days before due date, skip paid/under-500. All tests use fixed dates around holidays.json closing days.

fixture/docs/billing-notes.md holds the stale September rules (5 calendar days, every unpaid invoice) which are the trap to avoid; no hidden tests rely on paths or names not stated. The holidays.json is in config/ as expected.

The reviewer's own note shows the quick wrong answer (following the September notes) is caught: shallow/ scores 27.8 and session-1-only lazy/ 22.2 in the dry run.
